feed.headline: Mongolia hosts UN desertification summit as drought crisis deepens
feed.ai: Mongolia is hosting the UN Convention to Combat Desertification’s COP17 in Ulaanbaatar from 17 to 28 August, bringing together representatives from 196 countries and the European Union to tackle land degradation, drought and desertification.

feed.headline: Russia runs out of petrol at seven in 10 stations as fuel crisis worsens
feed.ai: Ukrainian drone campaign on Russia's energy infrastructure has caused fuel shortages so severe that the Kremlin has admitted it. Queues in Moscow are forming for the first time, and Russia has brought back banned low-grade fuel to plug the gap, while detaining residents who complained publicly.

feed.headline: Shootings surge as drug gangs torment Brussels
feed.ai: This year alone there have been more than 65 shootings in the Belgian capital, as drug crime soars.

feed.headline: Iceland holds knife-edge referendum on EU - and it could be decided on fish
feed.ai: On Saturday, Iceland will vote on EU membership talks, amid economic and geopolitical tensions.

feed.headline: Memory wars: Election clash over Germany's Nazi past as AfD eyes power in east
feed.ai: Remembering its role in the World Wars is a key aspect of modern Germany's identity but the AfD argues it is time to take a more positive view of the past.

feed.headline: 37 Killed Near Kyiv as Russian Drone Blitz Exposes Air Defense Gap
feed.ai: The strike, on a warehouse near Ukraine’s capital, came after days of attacks that strained air defenses and struck fear in civilians.

feed.headline: Icelanders Are Voting on E.U. Membership Talks. Here’s What to Know.
feed.ai: The Nordic nation is holding a referendum on Saturday on whether to start membership talks with the European Union. Voters are divided.

feed.headline: Why Iceland and Others Might Want In, Not Out, of the E.U. Club
feed.ai: A few years ago, some feared the European Union was going out of style. Now Iceland is mulling membership alongside a long list of candidates.

feed.headline: ‘The Sauna Is Hot and Uncomfortable’: Vote on E.U. Talks Makes Iceland Sweat
feed.ai: The usually genial country has been bitterly divided over a vote this weekend on whether to enter membership talks with the European Union.

feed.headline: Guinea-Bissau junta puts new constitution to referendum as opposition urges boycott
feed.ai: A commentator and a human rights activist, speaking to Euronews, stress that the law has already been published and call for stronger EU action.

feed.headline: Israeli activists protest outside EU offices in Jerusalem over Gaza war
feed.ai: Around a dozen Israeli activists gathered outside European Union representative offices in east Jerusalem on 28 August, calling on the bloc to take a stronger position on the war in Gaza.

feed.headline: Russia plans to mobilise 600,000 troops this year and next, Ukraine says
feed.ai: Ukrainian intelligence said Moscow has already decided to call up 300,000 this year and 300,000 in 2027, driven by massive losses and a collapse in voluntary recruitment. Kyiv expects the announcement to come after September's elections.
